'''Cumberland Gas Pipeline''' is an operating natural gas pipeline in the United States.<ref name="r63d212">{{Cite web|url=https://marcellusdrilling.com/2026/07/km-reports-tgp-cumberland-project-gas-pipe-in-tn-now-online/|title=KM Reports TGP Cumberland Project Gas Pipe in TN Now Online|website=marcellusdrilling.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="r30800f">{{Cite web|url=https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx|title=Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, U.S. Energy Information Administration, August 2026|website=eia.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline is located in Tennessee.<ref name="r63d212" />

==Background==
Tennessee Gas Pipeline built the Cumberland Pipeline to supply the Tennessee Valley Authority's new natural gas power plant at the site of the Cumberland Fossil Plant. The 30-inch pipeline is a 32-mile lateral. It starts at the company's existing 100 Line in Dickson County, Tennessee and ends at the power plant in Stewart County, Tennessee.<ref name="r63d212" /> Marcellus Drilling News reported in July 2026 that the roughly $235 million project was placed in service on May 26, 2026.<ref name="r63d212" />

In October 2024 a federal appeals court panel temporarily halted two permits needed to start construction. The panel's order delayed the start of work through Dickson, Houston and Stewart counties until the court decided the case.<ref name="rcc4b7c">{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241020193128/https://www.power-eng.com/gas/new-projects-gas/permits-put-on-hold-for-planned-pipeline-to-fuel-a-new-tennessee-natural-gas-power-plant/|title=Permits put on hold for planned pipeline to fuel a new Tennessee natural gas power plant|website=power-eng.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>
